blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (Path traversal in read_attachment bypasses the ticket authorization) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: CWE-22. `name` comes from the client and is joined to the ticket directory as is. An agent authorized on their own ticket 7 asks for `name="../42/invoice.pdf"` and reads an attachment of ticket 42, owned by another team, past the `may_read_ticket` check; `name="../../../../etc/passwd"` or an absolute `name="/etc/passwd"` (which makes `os.path.join` discard the base) reads any file the server process can read, including `helpdesk.db` with the API key digests. Validate the name where it enters: reject any value where `os.path.basename(name) != name` or that is `.`/`..`, or better, look the name up in the `attachments` table for that `ticket_id` and only then open it; additionally resolve the final path with `os.path.realpath` and check it stays under `os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, str(ticket_id))`. Add a test that a `../` name and an absolute name are refused.
findings.title: Path traversal in read_attachment bypasses the ticket authorization

findings.evidence:
def save_attachment(ticket_id: int, filename: str, data: bytes) -> str:
    """Stores an uploaded file under the ticket's directory; returns its name."""
    name = os.path.basename(filename)
    directory = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, str(ticket_id))
findings.recommendation: CWE-862. Unlike `read_attachment`, the upload operation takes no agent and checks nothing: if the handler that calls it (not in this change) does not check ownership itself, any authenticated agent can attach files to, or overwrite same-named attachments of, any team's ticket. Take `agent_id` and enforce `may_read_ticket` (or a write-specific check) inside `save_attachment`, as `read_attachment` does. Confidence low: the caller could not be seen.
findings.title: save_attachment performs no authorization check
